name: Hubbard Hall
use: Medium co-ed residence hall (about 210 students), first-year and upper-division; hosts the Transfer Community
architect: Griswold, Boyden, Wylde & Ames (builder: Franchi Brothers Construction Co.)

facts.text: Dedicated March 16, 1968 as a hall for female residents and named for trustee Austin I. Hubbard, a 1925 forestry graduate.
Designed by Griswold, Boyden, Wylde & Ames and built by Franchi Brothers Construction Company.
Housing lists it as a 210-student medium hall with traditional singles and doubles, home to the Transfer Community; meal plan required.

First floor has a study lounge with whiteboards, projector and fireplace, and a recreation lounge with pool table, piano and ping-pong; floor lounges at each end of upper floors, a community kitchen, laundry, dumbwaiter, hydration stations and a volleyball court.
Housing's accessibility list gives only roll-in building access and strobe alerts in some rooms; no elevator or air conditioning is listed.

s3.title: Ranking of UNH Dorms and Residence Halls

verdict: 1968 brick slab on concrete pilotis by Philbrook; plain, no A/C, decent rooms.
notes: No licensed photo found (Commons category and file search, Flickr search attempted). Reference photos: four-storey red-brick slab over a recessed, glazed ground floor behind a concrete band and columns; plain punched windows; room photo shows a standard double with bunked beds, a wide multi-pane window (good daylight for a dorm room) and an ordinary ~8 ft ceiling. Old row said 1967 and "Honors" theme: archives give only the 1968 dedication; Housing now lists the Transfer Community (Society19 Dec 2024 still calls it the honors dorm, possibly stale). No renovation found. Old row said bike storage and cable TV; Housing lists bike storage spaces but not cable.
judgeNotes: Reference photos show a utilitarian slab over an open ground floor.
